answer.evidence: The body is a 16px-wide outlined slab from row 1 to row 30. Below the small tan decor item on top (rows 0-3, width 7), rows 4-5 are only a light highlight. Row 6 is a gray seam line, and it matches the door seam at rows 13-14, so it reads as a door division rather than a front-edge line with eave shadow. The rows below are flat door faces with handles (the light strip at x=11, rows 16-24), a red label and a seam. There is no ellipse, no sloped plane and no visible contents. At most a 1-2 row highlight acts as a rim, so this is a flat front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The fridge is a small white/grey box with a thin outline, a freezer-door split, a small red label and two handles. The body is mostly flat near-white, with only about 3 lightness steps (light, mid grey, dark edge). 32% near-flat coverage is far above the references, which are 0-13% for the detailed ones (hedge 0%, cheese stall 13%, well 0%). There are 9 visible tones per tile, similar to the hedge. But those tones are spread across the outline, handles and label rather than carried as texture on the body, so the surface reads as a flat sticker-like fill. The outline is tinted (0% neutral dark edge), so it is not near-black. The well and cheese stall carry 17-20 visible tones with per-material grain, shaded stones and wood detail, and the fridge has no grain, speckle or panel shading to match them. It looks thinner and flatter than the references.
